8 Days in South Africa

The road trip you’ll regret not taking.
8 days self-drive + safari AED 11,129 per person coast, wine & big five

Cape Town → Stellenbosch → Route 62 → Garden Route → Knysna → Port Elizabeth → Safari in Hoedspruit. Eight days, and every single turn brought something we didn’t expect.

Penguins on a beach, whales off the cliffs, wine estates in the mountains, and the Big Five before breakfast — all on one tank-after-tank road trip.

by Wandering Stampers
before the itinerary

Africa changes you

We went for a holiday. We came back different people.

Nothing prepares you for standing in front of an elephant. Not a photo, not a documentary, not the hundred reels you’ve saved. You are simply small — and it is the most grounding feeling in the world. Every deadline you were losing sleep over goes quiet.

Then there are the roads. Hours of them, with the windows down and nowhere to be. And the sunsets — the kind that stop the car and the conversation, and hand your heart the exact peace you’ve been chasing for years without knowing its name.

Somewhere between the cliff roads of the Cape and a cold morning in an open jeep, the trip stopped being a trip. It became the thing we measure other trips against.

And fair warning: once you catch the safari bug, it never leaves. We were already planning our way back before we’d landed home.

Africa doesn’t give you a holiday. It gives you perspective — and then it ruins you for everywhere else.
how to use this guide

The route, and what it cost

Follow it day by day, or lift the bits you want. Each day lists the stops in the order we drove them with rough timings — the drives are the point here, so leave room for the pull-overs you’ll want to make.

what it cost us
AED 11,129
per person

Flights from Dubai, all stays, car rental, visa fees and the safari — everything in. Based on two people travelling together (AED 22,258 total).

one thing to plan around: the weather

South African weather is unpredictable — but it clears up just as quickly as it turns. On the road especially, cloud cover and rain can wipe out a stopover completely. Keep a spare day in hand so you can go back and try again.

getting there: take the direct flight

It’s a long haul from Dubai — there’s no pretending otherwise. But the direct flight to Cape Town was absolutely worth it: no connection, no airport dead time, and you land with the day still ahead of you. On a trip this tightly packed, the time you save is worth the fare difference.

The internal flights are a lovely surprise too — all 2-2 layout, so no middle seats and genuinely spacious. The hop up to Hoedspruit felt like part of the holiday rather than a chore.

the route at a glance
Day Base Highlights
1–2 Cape Town Penguins, Cape Point, Chapman’s Peak, Bo-Kaap
3 Stellenbosch Jordan Wine Estate · Franschhoek wine tram
4 Knysna Route 62 & the Garden Route — the big drive
5 Knysna Robberg Nature Reserve · Knysna loop
6 Port Elizabeth Tsitsikamma · Storms River Suspension Bridge
7–8 Hoedspruit All-inclusive safari — Big Five & luxury tents
1–2
day one & two
Cape Town
The Cape Peninsula loop
9 AM Muizenberg & St James — the row of candy-coloured beach huts. Ten minutes, one photo, entirely worth it.
11 AM Kalk Bay — seals loafing on the harbour wall, then lunch at Kalky’s (paper plates, no frills, brilliant).
1 PM ★ Boulders Beach — penguins. Actual wild penguins, waddling past your feet on a white-sand beach.
3 PM ★ Cape of Good Hope & Cape Point — take the funicular up, and eat at the Lighthouse Café with that view.
5 PM ★ Chapman’s Peak Drive — cliff-edge hairpins over the Atlantic. The drive of the whole trip.
7 PM Camps Bay for sunset — palm-lined strip, drinks with the Twelve Apostles behind you.
Day 2 Bo-Kaap — the painted houses and cobbled streets. Go early for empty light.
field note

Drive the peninsula anti-clockwise as above — you hit Chapman’s Peak with the sun going down over the water rather than in your eyes.

3
day three
Stellenbosch & Franschhoek
The winelands
11 AM ★ Jordan Wine Estate — tasting with vineyard-and-mountain views. Book the table, not just the tasting.
2 PM ★ Franschhoek wine tram — hop-on hop-off between estates, so nobody has to be the designated driver.

Timing · A slow, indulgent day. Estates close earlier than you’d think — start by 11 and you’ll fit three comfortably.

field note

One night here isn’t enough — see our mistakes page. If the Cape weather turns, a second night gives you a fighting chance at the views you came for.

4
day four
Route 62 & the Garden Route
Stellenbosch → Knysna
8 AM ★ Route 62 — the inland alternative to the coast road: mountain passes, farm stalls and almost no traffic.
1 PM ★ The Garden Route — forest, lagoon and sea all afternoon. Stop whenever it looks good; it always looks good.
6 PM Arrive Knysna — check in, eat oysters, sleep well.

Timing · A full driving day — leave early, and treat the stops as the itinerary rather than the interruption.

field note

Fill the tank whenever you’re under half on Route 62 — the gaps between towns are longer than they look on the map.

5–6
day five & six
Robberg, Tsitsikamma & Storms River
Knysna → Port Elizabeth
8 AM ★ Robberg Nature Reserve — a cliff-and-sea peninsula walk with seals below. Do it before the wind picks up.
2 PM Knysna day-trip loop — the Heads viewpoint, the waterfront, and a very slow lunch.
Day 6 ★ Tsitsikamma National Park — where the forest drops straight into the Indian Ocean.
11 AM ★ Storms River Suspension Bridge — the swaying walk over the river mouth. Short trail, big payoff.
4 PM Drive on to Port Elizabeth for the night, ready for the safari flight.

Timing · Robberg on the morning of day five (the full circuit is about 3 hours), then Tsitsikamma first thing on day six to beat the tour buses to the bridge, and an easy afternoon drive east.

field note

Proper shoes for Robberg — it’s rock and sand, not boardwalk, and there’s no shade on the point. And repack the night before Hoedspruit: that flight has a strict luggage allowance and steep fines.

7–8
day seven & eight
Safari, Hoedspruit
The grand finale
5:30 AM ★ Morning game drive — the best one. Coffee in the dark, then out as the bush wakes up.
4 PM ★ Sunset drive & the Big Five — sundowners in the middle of nowhere, then spotlights on the way back.
All in Luxury tents — all-inclusive: drives, every meal, and falling asleep to the sound of the bush.

Timing · Fly Port Elizabeth → Hoedspruit, then let the lodge run your day: two drives, three meals, nothing to plan.

field note

Two nights is the minimum — four drives gives you a real shot at all of the Big Five. Pack neutral colours and something genuinely warm; open vehicles at dawn are freezing.

the honest numbers

What eight days cost us

Two of us, everything included — flights from Dubai, the domestic hop to the safari, stays, the car, visa charges and the extras along the way.

What Notes AED
Flights Dubai return + domestic to Hoedspruit 10,369
Stays Airbnb · Alluvia · Agoda · safari lodge 9,002
Car rental + Dubai cab Cape Town → Port Elizabeth, one-way 1,575
Visa service fee e-visa attempt, then VFS submission 718
Additionals Fuel, park entries, food, wine tram 594
Total for two people 22,258
Per person everything included 11,129

Flights and stays swing hugely with season and how early you book — treat these as our real numbers, not a quote.

learn from us

Mistakes we’d avoid

01
give the wine estates more than one night

Cape weather is genuinely unpredictable — one night is one roll of the dice. Two gives you a backup day for the views and the long lunch you actually came for.

02
watch your luggage weight for the Hoedspruit flight

Small planes, strict allowances, steep fines. Weigh your bags the night before and shift the heavy things into your carry-on and DO NOT exceed the per baggage limit.

03
skip the e-visa — apply properly, and early

Ours simply didn’t process, and we ended up submitting passports at VFS anyway — paying twice and cutting it far too close. Apply for the proper visa well ahead.

this is the kind of road trip you’ll regret not taking.
